stories.title: Two NYPD Officers Revive Infant With CPR in Astoria
stories.dek: Officers Douglas Zimmerman and Jesutofunmi Aregbesola restored a 1-month-old boy's breathing in under two minutes after responding to a call in Queens, NY1 reported.
body: Two NYPD officers are being credited with saving the life of a 1-month-old boy in Astoria, Queens, after they responded to a call about an infant who was not breathing and had no pulse, according to NY1.

Officers Douglas Zimmerman and Jesutofunmi Aregbesola, who have each been on the job for about two years, worked together to revive the baby, the outlet reported. Zimmerman began the rescue effort, and Aregbesola then took over CPR. Their body-worn cameras recorded the response.

Less than two minutes after the officers arrived, the infant was breathing again, NY1 reported. Aregbesola told the outlet he saw the baby's eyes open and his color return, and said his academy training took over in the moment.
Zimmerman said that seconds matter when helping a child that young, according to the report.
About two weeks after the call, the officers said they had heard from the family that the baby was doing well, NY1 reported. The outlet did not say exactly when the rescue took place.

sources.title: Queens officers save baby's life in frantic CPR rescue

stories.title: Investigation Details Hourslong Ordeal for Six Nonverbal Students on School Bus
stories.dek: A school bus carrying six nonverbal students with special needs was taken to wrong locations around Brooklyn and arrived more than four hours late, a city investigator found, NY1 reported.
body: Six nonverbal students with special needs, ages 6 to 8, were unaccounted for for more than four hours last year after their school bus was taken to the wrong locations around Brooklyn, according to a report by the city's Special Commissioner of Investigation for the public schools, NY1 reported.

The students were due at school around 9 a.m. but did not arrive until about 1:25 p.m., the outlet said. A parent who had placed tracking devices in her two children's backpacks followed the bus and repeatedly called for information. School officials contacted the bus company at 10 a.m., and at 11:45 a.m. the company said the driver was lost but would arrive within 15 minutes. The bus arrived about an hour and 40 minutes later, after police had been called.

The bus was driven by a fill-in driver with less than three weeks on the job and staffed by a matron with nearly 20 years in the role, both employed by Consolidated Bus Transit, according to the report. The driver told investigators he went to two incorrect schools before getting the right address and was delayed by phone calls. The matron said she did not speak with the driver or try to contact anyone.

Special Commissioner Anastasia Coleman said the incident was serious enough to warrant a formal investigation, which recommended that the two employees no longer work with Department of Education students. The company told the Daily News both had been placed on administrative leave; it did not respond to NY1.
The city's yellow bus system serves about 150,000 children, nearly 70,000 of them with disabilities, NY1 reported.

sources.title: Investigation details hourslong ordeal for six students on school bus

stories.title: Brooklyn Conservatory of Music Opens Second Campus in Park Slope
stories.dek: The $17 million BKCM Prospect Park West facility will double the conservatory's capacity for music therapy and education, NY1 reported.
body: The Brooklyn Conservatory of Music has officially opened a second campus in Park Slope, according to NY1.

The new facility, called BKCM Prospect Park West, covers about 12,000 square feet and cost about $17 million to complete, the outlet reported. It includes a concert hall, a community space and music studios.

The expansion will double the conservatory's capacity for music therapy and music education, according to the report. The new building sits a few blocks from the conservatory's existing space, which has served the community for 129 years.
Adam Johnston, the conservatory's deputy executive director, discussed the expansion in an interview on NY1's weekend morning program, the outlet said.
NY1 did not report how the project was funded or detail the programs that will be offered at the new site.

sources.title: Brooklyn Conservatory of Music opens second campus

stories.title: New Charges Filed in Fentanyl Death of FIT Student
stories.dek: Federal authorities have added charges against a 19-year-old accused of giving two women fentanyl in a Fashion Institute of Technology dorm in March, NY1 reported.
body: A 19-year-old man accused in the fentanyl death of a Fashion Institute of Technology student faces new charges, including drug distribution with intent to commit rape, according to NY1, which cited prosecutors.

Prosecutors allege that in March 2026, Moises Freire gave two women fentanyl in a dorm room at the Manhattan college while telling them it was cocaine, and urged them to take it without taking any himself, NY1 reported. Both women quickly lost consciousness, according to the allegations.

Prosecutors further allege that Freire sexually assaulted one of the women and waited about 45 minutes before seeking help, the outlet said. Investigators say he falsely told campus security that the women had been drinking and passed out. Security officers administered Narcan. One woman survived; the other never regained consciousness and later died.

Freire and his alleged supplier, Brian Peralta Cabrera, also face drug conspiracy charges, according to the report. Christopher Roberts, special agent in charge of the Drug Enforcement Administration's New York office, said Freire had texted the supplier that the drug was poison, NY1 reported.

FIT told students in an email that it has strengthened safety protocols and training since the death and is adding security, the outlet said. NY1 did not report court dates or pleas. The charges are accusations, and both men are presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

sources.title: New charges in FIT student's fentanyl death, officials say

stories.title: Mamdani Asks Parking Lot and Garage Owners to Deny ICE Access
stories.dek: The mayor and more than 100 elected officials urged private operators not to let immigration agents use their properties as staging areas, NY1 reported.
body: Mayor Zohran Mamdani, leading a coalition of more than 100 state elected officials, has sent a letter urging private parking lot and garage operators across the five boroughs to keep federal immigration agents from using their properties as staging areas, according to NY1.

The letter asks owners not to rent, lend or otherwise make their facilities available to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, and to tell the agency directly that it is not allowed to use them, the outlet reported.

The request follows an Oct. 8 shooting in Marble Hill in which an ICE agent shot a 28-year-old man while his young son was in the car, NY1 reported. According to the mayor's office, agents had been using a privately owned parking lot a few blocks away as a staging area. The letter also cited reports of ICE using two bank parking lots on Northern Boulevard in Queens and a garage on Morton Street in Manhattan.

Mamdani argued that immigrants make up more than a third of the city's population and 43% of its workforce, and that businesses suffer when residents are afraid to drive or run errands, according to the report. He praised the Morton Street garage operator for removing ICE vehicles after neighbors raised concerns.

City law already restricts the use of city-owned property for federal civil immigration enforcement, but those limits do not apply in the same way to private property, the mayor's office said. NY1 did not include a response from ICE or parking industry representatives.

sources.title: Mamdani asks NYC parking lot, garage owners to deny ICE access

stories.title: Plaza Hotel to Close in January for Four-Year Renovation
stories.dek: The Fifth Avenue landmark will stop serving guests on Jan. 19 while its 119-year-old facade is repaired, NY1 reported, citing The New York Times.
body: The Plaza Hotel on Fifth Avenue will close to guests in January for a renovation expected to last four years, according to NY1, which cited a report in The New York Times.

The hotel's last day of service is scheduled for Jan. 19, 2027, with construction expected to begin the next day, NY1 reported. The project will focus on repairing the building's 119-year-old facade, according to the Times.
The Plaza is both a New York City landmark and a National Historic Landmark, so any work must follow historic preservation standards, the outlet noted.

The hotel has more than 300 employees, and no details have been released about their status during the closure, according to the report. It is also unclear how the construction will affect the building's full-time residents, NY1 said.

The Plaza last closed in 2005 for a major redevelopment that added more than 180 condominiums and more than 200 hotel rooms. The hotel has changed hands several times over its history, the outlet reported.

sources.title: Plaza Hotel to close in January for 4-year renovation, report says

stories.title: Hochul and Blakeman Clash Over Immigration and Trump in Governor's Debate
stories.dek: Gov. Kathy Hochul and Republican Bruce Blakeman spent much of their only scheduled debate attacking each other, City & State reported.
body: Gov. Kathy Hochul and her Republican challenger, Nassau County Executive Bruce Blakeman, met on Oct. 13 for the only scheduled debate of the governor's race, hosted by Spectrum News NY1 and moderated by Susan Arbetter and Errol Louis, according to City & State New York.

The candidates spent much of the hour responding to each other rather than to the moderators, the outlet reported. Hochul, who holds a comfortable lead in polls, mainly needed to avoid mistakes and appeared to do so, City & State said.

Immigration took up about 15 minutes after a recent shooting by an ICE agent in the city, according to the report. Hochul criticized federal agents' use of force and accused Blakeman of failing to condemn ICE. Blakeman blamed the state's sanctuary policies and said cooperation with federal authorities would have prevented such incidents.

Blakeman sought to rebut claims from Hochul's campaign that he is beholden to President Donald Trump, citing his support for abortion rights and a guest worker visa program, the outlet reported. Near the end, asked about reported remarks he made about Mayor Zohran Mamdani, Blakeman called the mayor antisemitic and tied Hochul to him.

Moderators also raised a 56% vacancy rate among prison workers after the 2025 wildcat strike, when Hochul fired more than 2,000 correction officers. Hochul defended the firings and the use of the National Guard, citing safety, according to City & State. Early voting begins Oct. 24, and Election Day is Nov. 3.

stories.title: Arturo O'Farrill Builds an East Harlem Home for Afro Latin Jazz
stories.dek: The Grammy-winning bandleader's nonprofit, Belongó, is raising money to finish Casa Belongó, a performance and education center under construction in East Harlem, NY1 reported.
body: Grammy-winning pianist, composer and bandleader Arturo O'Farrill is helping build a permanent cultural home for Afro Latin jazz in East Harlem, called Casa Belongó, according to NY1.

O'Farrill spoke with NY1 ahead of the annual benefit for his nonprofit, Belongó, which was held the Wednesday after the Oct. 12 interview. His Afro Latin Jazz Orchestra has also started a new weekly engagement in Times Square, the outlet reported.

According to a September press release from the organization, the benefit was set for Oct. 14 at City Winery on 11th Avenue in Manhattan, with proceeds supporting free music education in city public schools, community programs, free concerts and the completion of Casa Belongó. The center is under construction on Park Avenue at 118th Street, was designed by Diller Scofidio + Renfro and sits within the Timbale Terrace affordable housing development.

The program announced in the release included the premiere of a new O'Farrill composition blending the blues standard House of the Rising Sun with Afro-Cuban son, performances by Blues Brothers members Lou Marini and Leon Pendarvis, singer Daymé Arocena and the nonprofit's youth ensemble, the Fat Cats. Ballet Hispánico artistic director Eduardo Vilaro was named to receive the event's arts honor. Individual tickets started at $1,500.
Belongó was founded by O'Farrill in 2007 to perform, teach and preserve music of the Americas rooted in African and Indigenous traditions, according to the release.

sources.title: Arturo O'Farrill brings Afro Latin jazz to Harlem
Belongó's Second Annual Benefit October 14 at City Winery NYC

stories.title: James and Komatireddy Trade Attacks in Attorney General Debate
stories.dek: Attorney General Letitia James and Republican challenger Saritha Komatireddy met in their only debate before the Nov. 3 election, NY1 reported.
body: Democratic Attorney General Letitia James and her Republican challenger, Saritha Komatireddy, traded sharp attacks on Oct. 8 in their first and only debate before the Nov. 3 election, hosted by NY1, the outlet reported.

Komatireddy, a longtime federal prosecutor making her first run for office, called James a partisan who has used taxpayer money for political purposes during her eight years in office, according to NY1. She said James has never prosecuted a criminal case and accused her of prejudging an investigation into an alleged sexual assault at Cornell University. Komatireddy said she would prioritize cases involving mental illness and Medicaid fraud.

James responded that Komatireddy knows nothing about the attorney general's office, the outlet reported. She defended her earlier comments expressing solidarity with the alleged victim in the Cornell case as a show of empathy. Gov. Kathy Hochul had appointed James special prosecutor in that investigation the week before the debate.

James also said Komatireddy has not criticized the Trump administration and pointed to President Donald Trump's endorsement of her challenger as a sign she would not stand up to him, according to the report. Komatireddy stressed her service under President Barack Obama, said she had met Trump only briefly and said she would protect New Yorkers from political extremes on both sides.
The candidates shook hands at the end of the debate, NY1 reported.

sources.title: Attorney general candidates trade blows in fiery NY1 debate

stories.title: Neir's Tavern Marks 197 Years With Woodhaven Block Party
stories.dek: More than 700 people turned out on Oct. 3 as the historic Queens bar celebrated its anniversary and its owner signed a new 10-year lease, QNS reported.
body: Neir's Tavern celebrated its 197th anniversary with its annual block party on Saturday, Oct. 3, along 88th Avenue between 77th and 78th streets in Woodhaven, Queens, according to QNS.

The event drew more than 700 people and was sponsored by the Kiwanis Club of Ozone Park-Woodhaven, the outlet reported. Owner Loycent Gordon held a public, symbolic signing of the tavern's new 10-year lease, followed by a cake-cutting.

Gordon also presented the tavern's Ambassador Awards to six community members, including Rachel Kellner, owner of Aigner Chocolates, who received a small business award, and Kristen Guglielmo of the Queens Chronicle, who received the third annual Ruschell Boone Legacy Award, QNS reported. Gordon cited the tavern's motto, Community Conquers All.

Attendees played games including a steeplechase and a bouncy castle, and free hot dogs, cotton candy, popcorn and water were served, according to the report. A DJ played, and the group Soul Frequency performed and led a community dance. A raffle offered prizes including a limited-edition Queens Monopoly set.

Community Board 9, the Woodhaven Cultural and Historical Society, the Woodhaven Business Improvement District and State Sen. Joseph Addabbo Jr. were among those who helped organize the event, QNS said. The block of 78th Street outside the bar is also known as Neir's Tavern Way.

sources.title: Photos | Neir's Tavern in Woodhaven celebrates 197th anniversary during block party

stories.title: Westside Cowboy Plays Music Hall of Williamsburg
stories.dek: The Manchester indie rock band's Oct. 6 Brooklyn date opened a short run of U.S. headline shows after the release of its debut album, The Needle Drop reported.
body: Westside Cowboy, an indie rock band from Manchester, England, was scheduled to headline Music Hall of Williamsburg in Brooklyn on Tuesday, Oct. 6, according to The Needle Drop.

The show was the first of three U.S. dates announced in September, followed by The Foundry in Philadelphia on Oct. 10 and The Atlantis in Washington on Oct. 12, the outlet reported. They were the band's first American performances since the release of its debut album, It Goes On, on Island Records in August.

The band previously played small shows in Los Angeles and New York in December 2025, performing material from its earlier EPs, according to the report. Several dates on its UK and European tour have sold out, The Needle Drop said.
Tickets for the U.S. shows went on sale Sept. 11. The announcement did not list prices or age restrictions for the Brooklyn date.

sources.title: Westside Cowboy announce three USA shows on their headline tour

stories.title: Bronx Man, 68, Accused of Shooting Girlfriend and Another Man
stories.dek: A 70-year-old woman and a 60-year-old man were seriously wounded in a ninth-floor apartment on Third Avenue in the Bronx on Oct. 17, and a suspect was arrested, Hoy reported.
body: A 68-year-old Bronx man has been arrested and charged with attempted murder after a woman and a man were shot in an apartment on Third Avenue, according to the newspaper Hoy, citing authorities.

The shooting happened shortly before 9:30 p.m. on Saturday, Oct. 17, in a ninth-floor apartment at 3970 Third Avenue, at 173rd Street, the newspaper reported. The suspect, identified as Kenneth Morgan, allegedly shot his 70-year-old girlfriend and a 60-year-old man who was with her.

The woman was wounded in the abdomen and the man suffered several gunshot wounds to the chest, according to the report. Both were taken to a hospital in serious condition. Authorities did not release their names.
Hoy reported that the suspect barricaded himself inside an apartment before he was taken into custody. Investigators recovered several shell casings in the building's hallway, the newspaper said.

Morgan faces charges of attempted murder, assault, criminal possession of a weapon and reckless endangerment, according to the report. The charges are accusations, and he is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

sources.title: Tiroteo en El Bronx deja dos heridos graves y un detenido: el sospechoso se atrincheró en un apartamento

stories.title: Federal Jail Officer in Sunset Park Indicted in Contraband Bribery Case
stories.dek: A correctional officer at the Metropolitan Detention Center in Brooklyn is accused of taking cash from inmates' associates to smuggle contraband into the jail, federal prosecutors said.
body: A federal correctional officer at the Metropolitan Detention Center in Brooklyn has been indicted on charges that she took bribes to smuggle contraband into the Sunset Park jail, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of New York.

Melissa Brooks, 37, of Brooklyn, who has worked for the Federal Bureau of Prisons since July 2024, is charged with taking bribes as a public official and conspiracy to do so, prosecutors said. She was arrested on the morning of Oct. 14 and was scheduled to be arraigned that afternoon before U.S. Magistrate Judge James R. Cho.

Prosecutors allege that between July 2024 and December 2025, Brooks repeatedly accepted cash from associates of inmates in exchange for bringing contraband into the facility. On Oct. 18, 2024, she allegedly received $5,000 through a payment app from a person who had received the same amount minutes earlier from an inmate's relative, according to the release. In December 2025, she allegedly exchanged text messages with an inmate who was using a contraband phone.

U.S. Attorney Joseph Nocella Jr. said the alleged conduct endangered staff and inmates for personal gain, and officials with the Justice Department's inspector general and the FBI said they would keep pursuing corruption by prison staff.
If convicted of bribery, Brooks faces up to 15 years in prison, prosecutors said. The charges are allegations, and she is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

sources.outlet: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of New York
sources.title: Bureau of Prisons Correctional Officer Indicted for Bribery
